source: Radonjić et al., fixed-z shutters, Zenodo5775886. Authenticated 831 RAR members, 808 fixed-z files. Published negative tail direction at a chosen maximum and fitted phase, period and three-beam coupling exposed. All measured fixed-z powers numerically unopened before registration.
outcome: Third central moment of the signed pump sum, normalized by the fixed 1815 mW, globally centered at its uniform pooled mean over 101 cycles 640..740 and 500 replicates per state. Every cycle contributes 1/101. Compare actual paired index with all within-cycle couplings of the eight empirical marginals. No per-cycle recentering, exclusion, conditional subgroups or tuning.
scope: One power meter reads eight sequential shutter configurations, about one minute per cycle; every file header gives the same start epoch. No simultaneous counterfactual power or joint sampling law. Coupling-invariant mean from linearity. No repeat-trial independence, inference of an optical phase or statistical coverage.
method: Exact input decimals. Grid32 bins across widest signed marginal per cycle; each marginal uses its own minimum. Monotone cubed deviation gives lower and upper when floored and ceiled. Optimize over all empirical joint laws by partial-sum network flow enforcing exact marginals. Float LP suggests marginal duals; round to 1e-9 and repair worst slack over all reachable tuples using exact rational arithmetic. Retain all 202 certificates and all cycles. Bounds may be loose; never adjust grid postmeasurement.
controls: Original pairing, common signed ranks, eight single-reversed-rank permutations and conditional independence. Select per-cycle min/max attainable witnesses, then aggregate with predeclared weights. Strict one-sign outer bound certifies sign; attaining opposite signs proves ambiguity; otherwise unresolved. Sign of third central moment equals skewness sign with positive variance. No convex-order shortcut for a cubic. Report actual source roster vs published approximately 50,000, raw worst width cycle, stored statistic and applied limits. No point-phase or time-simultaneous optical forecast.
